Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Ayrton Warren, DOB: 16/05/1982, Gender: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Not recorded, Practice: GP at Hand, [Practice Address not recorded]. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (ongoing; currently stable; supported by transcript and DDx)
- Secondary: Work-related stress contributing to headaches (supported by transcript and DDx)
- Tertiary: Not recorded

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented), Paracetamol (single dose for headache; dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Allergies/ADRs: None known
- Past Medical History: Anxiety (~2 years duration); no hypertension; no other physical illnesses

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Anxiety (approx. 2 years)
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): Sertraline; no prior therapy or hospitalizations documented
- Family History: Mother with history of anxiety; no family history of migraines or other physical illnesses

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with partner
- Social Support: Not recorded
- Occupation/Education: Not recorded; significant work-related stress and backlog
- Alcohol Use: Not recorded
- Smoking/Substance Use: Non-smoker; no other substance use recorded
- Key Stressors: Work-related stress (ongoing for a couple of months, frequent late nights)

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Not recorded
- Mood & Affect: Not moody or angry; occasional frustration; mood "ebbs and flows"; no significant mood disorder features
- Speech & Thought: Not recorded
- Perception: No perceptual disturbances; no mention of hallucinations

Cognition:
- Orientation: Not recorded
- Attention/Concentration: Not recorded
- Memory: Not recorded
- Insight & Judgement: Insight present regarding stress and workload; judgment appears intact

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Disturbed (frequent late nights); advised to optimize sleep
- Appetite: Not recorded
- Motivation/Energy: Not recorded
- Anxiety Symptoms: Mild, situational (work-related); generally manageable; no panic, no major functional impact currently

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicidality
- Protective Factors: Stable home environment (partner); insight into symptoms; seeking help
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
The patient, with a background of anxiety (stable on Sertraline), is experiencing exacerbation of tension and migraine symptoms triggered by recent, sustained work-related stress and sleep disruption. Predisposing factors include personal and family history of anxiety. Precipitating factors are current work stress and backlog. Perpetuating factors include lack of adequate sleep and high demands at work. Protective factors include supportive home environment and engagement with primary care.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (stable, stress-exacerbated headaches)
- Patient Goal(s): Manage stress; maintain mental health stability
- Clinical Goal(s): Minimize anxiety exacerbations; support stress management; monitor and treat associated headaches
- Actions (Patient):
  - Consider reducing workload or taking time off work
  - Engage with counseling services (link to be provided)
  - Implement sleep hygiene; increase hydration (aim for 1.5–2 liters fluids per day)
  - Continue prescribed Sertraline
  - Monitor and record headache patterns and stress triggers
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide information and referral link to local counseling services
  - Recommend self-certification for at least one week off work if needed
  - Provide patient education regarding stress management, sleep, and hydration
  - Arrange follow-up in one week
  - Prescribe or recommend first-line analgesia for headache management (Ibuprofen/Aspirin advice per guidelines)
  - Provide written information on warning signs for headaches and when to seek urgent care

Secondary Problem: Work-related Stress
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce and better manage work stress
- Clinical Goal(s): Address psycho-social contributors to anxiety and headaches; prevent escalation of stress-related symptoms
- Actions (Patient):
  - Utilize counseling and stress reduction techniques
  - Discuss workload adjustments with employer if willing
  - Optimize exercise routine as feasible (patient runs 3x/week)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Encourage and enable access to mental health/counseling supports
  - Reassess impact of stress on mental health and headaches at follow-up

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Danger signs/symptoms of headaches; stress management strategies; sleep hygiene; hydration; counseling resources; when to seek urgent review
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Return or escalation of severe headaches; significant increase in anxiety or mood changes; thoughts of self-harm; any danger symptoms as per written summary
- Coping Strategies: Counseling/therapy referral; workload adjustments; regular physical activity; maintaining sleep hygiene; supportive relationships

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded (referral to be made)
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: 1 week (as arranged for follow-up)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine: High likelihood. Sudden, severe one-sided headache with photophobia and triggers of stress/sleep deprivation; most consistent with current episode.
- Tension-type headache: Medium likelihood. Prior headaches associated with stress/anxiety, but atypical for current severity and lateralization.
- Dehydration/sleep deprivation: Low likelihood. Recent late nights and stress may contribute; not sole explanation due to severity and acuity.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Gender, contact details, social support, occupation specifics, alcohol use, appetite, motivation documented; several MSE/cognition elements not recorded (remote consult context).  
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted; DDx and transcript agree on nature of anxiety, stress, and headache etiology.  
● Transcript quality notes: Complete, good quality; structured telemedicine encounter with relevant clinical and mental health history.
